findings.section: 1. When you play, and what differs between the hours
findings.claim: The 165 games started between 01:00 and 06:59 are concentrated in a few episodes (90 in 2025-12) and look like late nights rather than travel.
findings.metric: number of standard live games with local start hour 1-6 (Europe/London)
findings.caveat: If the player did travel, the hour labels of those games are wrong.

findings.section: 1. When you play, and what differs between the hours
findings.claim: The night band (0-6) is 80% bullet and 52% from 2025-26, so its games differ in time class and era from the other bands.
findings.metric: share of night-band games (280 games) that are bullet
findings.caveat: Hours are not assigned at random; time class, rating and year are controlled in section 5 but the reason for playing late is not.

findings.section: 1. When you play, and what differs between the hours
findings.claim: 29% of the games are played at the weekend (Sat 790, Sun 931 of 6,027).
findings.metric: share of games started on Saturday or Sunday

findings.section: 1. When you play, and what differs between the hours
findings.claim: 109 of 1,500 sessions span more than one hour band (817 games); each game is assigned to the band of its own start time.
findings.metric: number of sessions (30-minute gap) whose games start in more than one hour band
findings.caveat: CIs are clustered by session, which is conservative for between-band comparisons.

findings.section: 2. Hour by hour, all time classes pooled
findings.claim: Across the 19 hourly buckets, score minus model expectation spans 0.135 points per game, from -0.057 (hour 22) to 0.077 (hour 9), with the CI excluding zero in only one bucket.
findings.metric: range of per-hour mean score minus the calibration model's move-1 expectation
findings.caveat: With 19 buckets about one CI excluding zero is expected by chance.

findings.section: 2. Hour by hour, all time classes pooled
findings.claim: Games started at 9:00 local time score above the model's expectation, the only hourly bucket whose CI excludes zero.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, games started in hour 9
findings.caveat: One of 19 buckets; about one such cell is expected by chance.

findings.section: 2. Hour by hour, all time classes pooled
findings.claim: Games started at 22:00 have the lowest hourly score minus expectation, with a CI that just includes zero.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, games started in hour 22
findings.caveat: One of 19 buckets; the paired ep gap at hour 22 is -0.0003 [-0.0013, 0.0010], i.e. the player did not err more than the opponents.

findings.section: 2. Hour by hour, all time classes pooled
findings.claim: At hour 9 the player loses fewer expected points per move than the opponents in the same games; this and hour 13 are the only two of 19 hourly paired gaps whose CI excludes zero.
findings.metric: player minus opponents ep_loss per move, move-weighted, games started in hour 9
findings.caveat: With 19 buckets, about one such cell is expected by chance.

findings.section: 2. Hour by hour, all time classes pooled
findings.claim: The player's and the opponents' ep lost per move move together hour by hour (correlation 0.91 across buckets): the hour changes the games, not the player alone.
findings.metric: correlation across 19 hour buckets between player ep_loss per move and opponents' ep_loss per move

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Raw late-evening games (21-23) score 0.046 points per game below the rest, with a CI that just includes zero.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, late 21-23 band minus all other bands
findings.caveat: Raw contrast without controls; the sessions that run late are the ones that were going well or badly enough to continue. The regression coefficient is -0.023 [-0.071, 0.020].

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: In late-evening games (21-23) the player's error rate is indistinguishable from the opponents' in the same games; the opponents' error moves with the player's.
findings.metric: ep_loss per move, player vs opponents, late 21-23 band, paired difference
findings.caveat: The band − other bands contrast on the paired gap is 0.0007 [-0.0001, 0.0014].

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: The share of the player's losses that were on time is slightly higher in late-evening games than in the rest, within the CI.
findings.metric: flags / your losses, late 21-23 band minus all other bands
findings.caveat: The difference is the band − other bands contrast on the player's flag share; the opponents' value is their own flag share of their losses in the same band. The late band is 70% bullet, where flagging is common.

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Night games (0-6) score the same as the rest relative to the model's expectation.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, night 0-6 band minus all other bands
findings.caveat: Night games are 80% bullet and cluster in a few episodes; without the 2025-12 episode the band has 157 games (section 6).

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Night games are played about a second per move faster than the rest, because the night band is mostly bullet.
findings.metric: your seconds per move, night 0-6 band minus all other bands
findings.caveat: Seconds per move pool time controls within a class; compare within a time class only. Within bullet the contrast is 0.15 [-0.02, 0.35].

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Midday games (12-14) score above the rest relative to expectation, one of 3 of 46 band contrasts whose CI excludes zero.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, midday 12-14 band minus all other bands
findings.caveat: About 2 of 46 contrasts are expected to exclude zero by chance; not stable across eras (0.082 [0.038, 0.124] in 2021-2023 vs -0.012 [-0.066, 0.038] in 2024-2026).

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: In midday games (12-14) the player loses slightly fewer expected points per move than the opponents in the same games.
findings.metric: ep_loss per move, player vs opponents, midday 12-14 band, paired difference
findings.caveat: The band − other bands contrast on the gap is -0.0007 [-0.0014, 0.0000]; the effect is confined to 2021-2023 (section 6).

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Of the 46 band-vs-rest contrasts on score minus expectation and the paired ep gap, 3 exclude zero, about the 2 expected by chance.
findings.metric: number of band − other bands contrasts (score − expectation and paired ep gap, 4 classes × 6 bands) whose 95% CI excludes zero
findings.caveat: Cells with fewer than 20 games are blank (rapid night).

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Blitz games at midday (12-14) score above the other blitz games relative to expectation.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, blitz midday 12-14 band minus other blitz bands
findings.caveat: One of 3 of 46 contrasts excluding zero, about 2 expected by chance.

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: In blitz evening games (18-20) the player's paired ep gap to the opponents is slightly worse than in other blitz games.
findings.metric: player minus opponents ep_loss per move, blitz evening 18-20 band minus other blitz bands
findings.caveat: One of 3 of 46 contrasts excluding zero, about 2 expected by chance; the within-band paired gap is 0.0007 [-0.0001, 0.0016].

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Blitz afternoon games (15-17) have fewer errors per move by both the player and the opponents than other blitz games, so the pool rather than the player differs.
findings.metric: ep_loss per move, blitz afternoon 15-17 band minus other blitz bands, player (difference) and opponents
findings.caveat: player and opponents here are each side's band − other bands contrast; difference is the contrast on the paired gap.

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Late-evening bullet games (21-23) score below other bullet games relative to expectation, within the CI.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, bullet late 21-23 band minus other bullet bands
findings.caveat: Paired ep gap contrast 0.0005 [-0.0004, 0.0014].

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Late-evening blitz games (21-23) score below other blitz games relative to expectation, within the CI.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, blitz late 21-23 band minus other blitz bands
findings.caveat: Paired ep gap contrast 0.0014 [-0.0001, 0.0030].

findings.section: 3. Hour bands by time class
findings.claim: Late-evening rapid games (21-23) score the same as other rapid games relative to expectation.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, rapid late 21-23 band minus other rapid bands
findings.caveat: Small cell (40 games); the rapid night band (12 games) is blank.

findings.section: 4. Day of the week, and weekday × hour band
findings.claim: Thursday is the only weekday whose score minus expectation CI excludes zero; weekdays run from -0.008 (Tuesday) to 0.047 (Thursday).
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, games started on Thursday
findings.caveat: One of 7 weekdays; a few CIs excluding zero are expected by chance across the many cells.

findings.section: 4. Day of the week, and weekday × hour band
findings.claim: On Thursdays the player loses marginally fewer expected points per move than the opponents, the only weekday where the paired gap's CI touches zero.
findings.metric: ep_loss per move, player vs opponents, Thursday games, paired difference
findings.caveat: Upper CI bound is -0.0000; one of 7 weekdays.

findings.section: 4. Day of the week, and weekday × hour band
findings.claim: Weekend games score the same as weekday games relative to the model's expectation.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, weekend minus weekday, all classes
findings.caveat: The regression's weekend coefficient with controls is -0.001 [-0.033, 0.030].

findings.section: 4. Day of the week, and weekday × hour band
findings.claim: The paired player-minus-opponents ep gap does not differ between weekend and weekday games.
findings.metric: player minus opponents ep_loss per move, weekend minus weekday, all classes
findings.caveat: Both sides lose about 0.0010 more ep per move at the weekend (yours 0.0010 [-0.0008, 0.0029], theirs 0.0011 [-0.0006, 0.0029]), i.e. the pool, not the player.

findings.section: 4. Day of the week, and weekday × hour band
findings.claim: The share of the player's losses on time is the same at the weekend as on weekdays.
findings.metric: flags / your losses, weekend minus weekday, all classes

findings.section: 4. Day of the week, and weekday × hour band
findings.claim: Weekend evenings (18-23) and weekday nights (21-06) score the same relative to expectation.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, weekend evening 18-23 minus weekday night 21-06
findings.caveat: player is the weekend-evening value, opponents the weekday-night value (both the player's own score − expectation); paired ep gap difference -0.0004 [-0.0015, 0.0007].

findings.section: Weekday × hour band
findings.claim: Weekend late-evening games (21-23) have the lowest cell in the day-type × band grid, with a CI that just includes zero.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, weekend × late 21-23 cell
findings.caveat: One of 12 day-type × band cells; paired ep gap in the cell 0.0006 [-0.0008, 0.0019].

findings.section: Weekday × hour band
findings.claim: Weekend evening games (18-20) score above the model's expectation, one of two day-type × band cells whose CI excludes zero (with weekend midday).
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, weekend × evening 18-20 cell
findings.caveat: Many cells (42 in the full grid); a few CIs excluding zero are expected by chance.

findings.section: 4. Day of the week, and weekday × hour band
findings.claim: Rapid games on Sundays score well above expectation and show the largest paired ep gap in the player's favour of any weekday cell.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, rapid games started on Sunday
findings.caveat: difference is the paired player − opponents ep gap per move (negative favours the player). Small cell among 21 weekday × class cells; chance hits are expected.

findings.section: 5. Regression with session, time-class and era controls
findings.claim: With session, time-class, rating and year controls, late-evening games (21-23) do not score differently from afternoon games.
findings.metric: OLS coefficient of late 21-23 band on score − model expectation (reference afternoon 15-17), session-bootstrapped CI
findings.caveat: Pooled between-session model; the reason for still playing at 23:00 is not controlled.

findings.section: 5. Regression with session, time-class and era controls
findings.claim: With controls, midday games (12-14) have the largest band coefficient on score minus expectation, but its CI includes zero.
findings.metric: OLS coefficient of midday 12-14 band on score − model expectation (reference afternoon 15-17)
findings.caveat: Band coefficients on score range from -0.023 to +0.037; permutation p 0.46 for the band block.

findings.section: 5. Regression with session, time-class and era controls
findings.claim: With controls, night games (0-6) score the same as afternoon games.
findings.metric: OLS coefficient of night 0-6 band on score − model expectation (reference afternoon 15-17)

findings.section: 5. Regression with session, time-class and era controls
findings.claim: The midday band coefficient on the paired ep gap is the only hour-band coefficient in the regression whose CI excludes zero, and it is not stable across eras.
findings.metric: OLS coefficient of midday 12-14 band on player − opponents ep_loss per move (reference afternoon 15-17)
findings.caveat: Best read as one of the chance hits a 46-contrast table produces: -0.0015 [-0.0023, -0.0007] in 2021-2023 vs 0.0000 [-0.0008, 0.0008] in 2024-2026.

findings.section: 5. Regression with session, time-class and era controls
findings.claim: With controls, weekend games score the same as weekday games.
findings.metric: OLS coefficient of weekend dummy on score − model expectation

findings.section: 5. Regression with session, time-class and era controls
findings.claim: A session-level permutation test finds the five hour-band coefficients on score minus expectation no larger than if the hour carried no information.
findings.metric: permutation p-value (max absolute band coefficient, 300 session-level shuffles of band labels) for score − model expectation
findings.caveat: Sum-of-squares p is 0.50; this joint test is the headline test because the many cells produce chance hits.

findings.section: 5. Regression with session, time-class and era controls
findings.claim: The hour-band block is jointly uninformative for the paired player-minus-opponents ep gap under a session-level permutation test.
findings.metric: permutation p-value (max absolute band coefficient) for player − opponents ep_loss per move
findings.caveat: Sum-of-squares p is 0.23; for your ep per move alone the max p is 0.74, for losing on time 0.90.

findings.section: 5. Regression with session, time-class and era controls
findings.claim: In the same model, the last game of a session scores 0.187 points below expectation, an order of magnitude larger than any hour-band coefficient.
findings.metric: OLS coefficient of last-game-of-session dummy on score − model expectation, same regression as the hour bands
findings.stake_note: Regression coefficient on score − expectation for the last game of a session; shown for scale against the hour bands. Q5 owns this finding and its selection caveats.
findings.caveat: Score − expectation in late-session games is positively selected between sessions (Q5); the stopping rule means a loss ends the session more often.

findings.section: 5. Regression with session, time-class and era controls
findings.claim: In the same model, the game after a loss scores 0.053 points below expectation, larger than any hour-band coefficient.
findings.metric: OLS coefficient of previous-game-lost dummy on score − model expectation, same regression as the hour bands
findings.stake_note: Regression coefficient on score − expectation for the game after a loss; shown for scale against the hour bands. Previous game won is -0.013 [-0.050, 0.022].
findings.caveat: Pooled between-session model; Q5 is the owner of the tilt finding.

findings.section: 6. Stability checks
findings.claim: The midday score advantage exists only in 2021-2023 and vanishes in 2024-2026.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, midday 12-14 band, 2021–2023 (player) vs 2024–2026 (opponents field)
findings.caveat: opponents here holds the 2024–2026 value of the same player metric, not the opponents' number.

findings.section: 6. Stability checks
findings.claim: The sign of the raw band effect on score minus expectation agrees between the two halves of the history in only 2 of the 6 bands.
findings.metric: number of hour bands whose score − expectation has the same sign in 2021–2023 and 2024–2026
findings.caveat: Night band has 79 games in 2021–2023.

findings.section: 6. Stability checks
findings.claim: Dropping the largest late-night episode (2025-12, 90 games) leaves the night band's score minus expectation unchanged near zero.
findings.metric: score minus model expectation, night 0-6 band without 2025-12 (player) vs all other bands (opponents field)
findings.caveat: opponents here holds the other-bands value of the same player metric. Paired ep gap in the reduced night band is -0.0004 [-0.0020, 0.0015].
